hypothesis: the O-antigen axis is the systematic weak point of the serotyping cells, as suggested by the Salmonella serovar result (H often right where O failed)
why: the O antigen resolves on 87.3% of scoreable isolates against the H antigen's 98.7% (gap +0.113) -- the same asymmetry seen in the Salmonella cell, on an independent cell with a different allele database. The weakness travels with the O-antigen axis, not with one caller.
honest_limits: NO IN-SILICO INCUMBENT: NCBI-PD does not populate `computed_types` for E. coli, so unlike the Salmonella cell there is no comparator and the ABSOLUTE accuracy here is much less interpretable. The internally-controlled O-vs-H contrast is what this run supports.

The label is PD's submitter `serovar` parsed to a strict O:H shape. E. coli O:H serotyping is traditionally agglutination-based, but per-isolate provenance is unprovable here and -- unlike the Salmonella run -- there is no incumbent score to use as a circularity probe.

O-only labels are scored on the O axis alone; they cannot score H. The two axes therefore have DIFFERENT denominators, which is why resolved-rate and accuracy are reported per axis rather than pooled.
'H-' (non-motile) is a MEANINGFUL label, not a missing value, and is scored as such.
Per-O-group and per-BioProject caps deliberately flatten prevalence away from O157.

selection_rule_fix.defect: coverage-only allele selection (the SAME defect the sibling Salmonella caller had already fixed with identity-primary, never propagated here)
selection_rule_fix.mechanism: fliC flagellin alleles cross-hybridize at near-full COVERAGE across antigen types, so a coverage tiebreak picks the wrong antigen while looking confident
selection_rule_fix.confirmed_by: code inspection of dna_decode/serotype/runner.py before the change, not inferred from the numbers alone
selection_rule_fix.resolution_unchanged: the fix changes WHICH allele is picked, not WHETHER one is -- no_call counts are identical

same_pattern_present_elsewhere_NOT_fixed.why_not_fixed: no wet-lab validation cohort exists for either, and the biology differs (whole-locus cps reference matching / Inc replicon families vs per-antigen flagellin alleles), so identity-primary is NOT automatically correct there. Changing them blind would be an unvalidated behaviour change.
